transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, I’m here because this has been going on at work for, I’d say, over a year now, and I feel like every time I try to explain it, people act like I’m making connections that aren’t there. But from my side, the pattern is pretty clear.

I work in computer support, and there was this new ticket rotation they put in, along with these security audits, and on paper they keep saying it’s just “policy” or “standard procedure.” Management has even shown me logs and reports and said, “See, this is all normal,” but to me it looks like they’re using the rotation and the audits to build a paper trail against me. Like they’re assigning certain tickets or reviewing certain actions in a way that makes it look like I’m the problem, so later they can point to it and say there was a history.

I’ve tried to get someone to take it seriously, but it’s always explained away. That’s really what brought me in—I’m tired of being treated like I’m overreacting when this has been happening for more than a year.
Aside from these suspicions about work, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see?

No, not really. I mean, I don’t hear voices talking to me or anything like that, and I haven’t seen, you know, people or things that aren’t there. It’s not like that.

Sometimes at work I’ll notice sounds or little things happening and wonder if they’re connected to what’s going on, but that’s different from hearing something nobody else can hear. I’m talking about things that are actually happening—tickets being assigned, audits being done, people saying certain things—not visions or voices. So, no, I wouldn’t say I’ve had that.

Outside of work, do you generally find yourself distrustful or suspicious of people close to you—like friends, family, or partners—feeling they might be trying to deceive or harm you, even in situations unrelated to your job?

I don’t think so, no—not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I can be cautious, sure, especially after dealing with what’s been happening at work, but with my family or people I’ve known a long time, I don’t sit around thinking they’re plotting against me or trying to hurt me.

Sometimes I might wonder if people really understand what I’m saying, or if they’re just trying to smooth things over because they don’t want to get involved, but that feels different than thinking they’re deceiving me. I wouldn’t say I’m suspicious of everyone in my life. It’s really centered around the work situation and the people involved there.

Aside from the situation at work, have you noticed any changes in your day-to-day functioning—like your ability to take care of yourself, keep up with daily responsibilities, or maintain relationships—since this all started?

No, I don’t think so—not in the basic day-to-day way. I mean, I’m still taking care of the house, keeping things in order, paying the bills on time, doing the normal responsibilities. I help my wife with things around the house, errands, whatever needs doing. It’s not like I’ve stopped functioning or let everything fall apart.

And at work, that’s part of why this is so frustrating to me. I can still do the technical side of the job. I handle the computer support work, I troubleshoot, I close tickets, I do what I’m supposed to do. Nobody’s really saying, “Your work is sloppy,” or “You’re disorganized,” at least not in a straightforward way. That’s why the ticket rotation and the audits bother me so much, because outside of that issue, I’m not falling apart or unable to do my responsibilities.

Relationships-wise, I mean, this has been stressful to talk about, especially when people don’t seem to understand why I’m concerned, but I still maintain my relationships. I still have my home life. I’m not neglecting everything. The main disruption is how much mental space this work situation takes up, but in terms of daily functioning, I’d say I’m still managing.
